title: Inference Inspector: metrics conductor for tenant-aware OTLP/Prometheus handoff
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a lightweight 'metrics conductor' component that sits between inference-side telemetry producers and our existing OTLP/Prometheus ingestion plane. The conductor's responsibilities are: deterministic sharding of tenant streams for Prometheus remote_write and OTLP exporters, prefix-aware label canonicalization for inference KPIs (model, route, container, kv-cache-hit), adaptive batching to respect per-tenant latency SLOs, and a durable staging path for bursts (short-term buffer). This ticket covers design + prototype + integration tests for the conductor and a small runtime sidecar shim to be deployed on Dedicated and Private nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype conductor accepts OTLP/gRPC and HTTP Prometheus remote_write from sidecars and forwards to our ingestion gateway with preserved tenant_id and canonical labels
Deterministic sharding: same tenant -> same shard 99.99% of the time across restarts (stable hashing with salt rollout)
Adaptive batching keeps 95th percentile producer-side observed tail latency increase < 5ms for p50 < 30ms workloads (load test verified)
Durable staging persists up to 30s of burst traffic without metric loss at 100k rps equivalent ingestion (integration test)
End-to-end dashboards show correct breakdown per-tenant, per-model, and per-route; alerts fire on >1% metric drop vs synthetic traffic within 5 minutes
Security: conductor uses TLS mutual auth to upstream exporters and honors tenant-level ACLs (integration test with KMS token)
Documentation: runbook and deployment guide for Dedicated/Private packages merged to Confluence and referenced in PR
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha: Kickoff: drafted RFC and shared with telemetry and serving runtime. Highlighted need for deterministic sharding to make Prometheus rollup stable across restarts.

2026-03-04 - Diego: Spike completed for stable-hash algorithm (murmur3+salt) and proto for tenant header propagation. Found edge-case where ephemeral container IDs were leaking into labels; added canonicalizer step.
2026-03-05 - Review (PM: Linh Tran): Confirmed customer-facing SLO targets. Suggested adding per-tenant burst quota gating to protect shared ingestion. Marked for security review.

2026-03-06 - Design review notes: prefer push-based path for low-cardinality tenant metrics and hybrid push/pull for per-route high-cardinality KPIs. Agreed to use short-lived durable staging (RocksDB-backed queue) rather than Kafka to simplify Private deployment.
2026-03-07 - Prototype PR opened: implementation includes gRPC OTLP ingress, deterministic shard mapper, label canonicalizer, batching window, and remote_write multiplexor. Initial unit tests added.

2026-03-09 - Load test (Diego): ran synthetic traffic simulating 2k tenants and heavy burst patterns. Observed 99th percentile staging ack latency 420ms under worst-case burst; tuning batching window reduced it to 180ms.
2026-03-10 - Security (Priya Joshi): requested mutual-TLS enforcement and token rotation support. Also asked for KMS integration tests; added to acceptance criteria.
notes: Trade-offs: RocksDB-staging chosen to avoid adding Kafka operational burden to Private deployments; trade is local disk durability vs central replayability.
Label canonicalization will use a whitelist approach: map high-cardinality ephemeral labels (container_id) -> container_slot and drop raw IDs unless requested by tenant opt-in.
Sharding salt rollout: support a two-phase rollout (read-only salt + migrate window) to avoid global re-sharding churn when changing salt value.
Cost impact: adaptive batching expected to reduce token-cost-attribution noise and cut ingestion TPS by ~15% for bursty workloads per estimator in RFC.
